evidence_items.explanation: Cursor limited included frontier-model use on its Pro plan in June 2025. This is one instance of the austerity he describes. It does not show prevalence.

receipt.public_excerpt: The user message model also isn’t sustainable for Augment Code as a business.

evidence_items.explanation: Augment moved to credit pricing because of costs, which fits 'had to'. It is one more instance, not proof that most startups did the same.

receipt.public_excerpt: McClernan argued that usage-based pricing is "fast becoming the industry standard," referencing pricing changes from competitors including Zed, Replit, Cursor, and Anthropic.

evidence_items.explanation: A trend report naming several coding-tool startups that changed pricing. It suggests a broad shift in coding tools, but it is one CEO's description, not a survey of all AI startups.

unresolved_gaps: No survey or representative dataset of AI startup pricing changes from June to December 2025 was found, so 'just about every' cannot be measured.
Examples cluster in AI coding tools. Evidence for other AI startup categories was not found.
Whether each change was forced by cost ('had to') or chosen is shown only for Augment.
